content.title: About
content.content: Breadsticks are soft, aromatic dough pieces prepared in fast‑food outlets or restaurants. They are usually served as long, thin sticks, often sprinkled with cheese, herbs, or spices. Their tender texture makes them perfect for dipping into sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Breadsticks are a common appetizer in Italian restaurants, served alongside pasta and sauces.
There are many variations: garlic, parmesan, sesame‑seed, or herb‑infused versions.
In the United States they are often marketed as "soft pretzel sticks" and sold in fast‑food chains.
Traditionally the dough is made from wheat flour, yeast, water, salt, and a small amount of sugar.
Breadsticks can be a standalone snack or part of combo meals.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Breadsticks provide quickly digestible carbs that supply energy for active lifestyles.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: When made with whole‑grain flour they deliver B1, B2, and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike fried snacks, soft breadsticks are typically baked without large amounts of oil.

items.title: Fiber content
items.content: Using whole‑grain flour increases dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: Breadsticks pair easily with vegetable, cheese, or protein‑rich dips, allowing a varied diet.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Breadsticks contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because of rapid carbohydrate absorption, they can cause a quick blood‑sugar spike, which is relevant for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salted varieties may contain significant sodium; those monitoring salt intake should choose unsalted options.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although less calorie‑dense than fried snacks, overconsumption can still lead to excess calorie intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve breadsticks warm and dip them in sauces such as marinara, cheese, garlic aioli, yogurt, or avocado. They can be cut into pieces for salads, soups, or used as a base for mini‑sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep breadsticks in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate them; they stay soft for about a week. Reheat in the oven for 5‑7 minutes before serving to restore aroma.
